column2: 'For teams selling to other businesses. Siro captures every meeting, from the first visit to the final decision, and keeps each account’s history in one place.' (In their office card); 'Siro’s science comes from each seller’s own conversations.' (https://www.siro.ai/)
column3: 'brings sales data and insights in the flow of work' (hero); CRM data surfaced inside Microsoft 365, no memory language (https://adoption.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot-for-sales/)
column4: 'Let agents pursue goals across days and weeks, retain context, adapt their plans, and complete multi-touch workflows with human oversight.'; 'Route work, share context, and coordinate specialized agents across complex customer and operational journeys.'; 'grounded in Data 360 and Customer 360, so every agent knows the customer before it says a word' (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/); 'Revenue breaks where context goes.' and 'capturing buyer intent, preserving it across every handoff' (https://www.salesforce.com/sales/)
column5: 'Fathom gives teams a shared source of truth across every customer conversation, internal sync, and strategy call' ('Fathom for teams' tab) (https://www.fathom.ai/); card heading 'Perfect prospect memory' (https://www.fathom.ai/solutions/sales)
column6: 'Otter transcribes every meeting, turning it into searchable knowledge that powers your workflow.' (hero); 'The world's only Conversational Knowledge Engine' (closing CTA) (https://otter.ai/)
column7: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column8: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all five ground their value in accumulated conversation or customer context on the inspected pages (Siro: account history kept 'in one place' and coaching built from each seller's own conversations; Microsoft: CRM data in the Microsoft 365 flow of work; Salesforce: agents that retain and share context, grounded in Data 360 and Customer 360; Fathom: a 'shared source of truth' across conversations; Otter: 'searchable knowledge' and a 'Conversational Knowledge Engine'). Difference: Salesforce treats memory as platform data feeding agents, and its Sales page now names context loss as the revenue problem; Fathom and Otter treat it as a searchable meeting archive; Siro scopes it to field-sales conversations; Microsoft's adoption page uses no memory language. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): memory and knowledge language is now claimed by two notetakers and by Salesforce, so the word alone is unlikely to differentiate; test whether CROs distinguish one memory that links calls, practice and content from a transcript archive or a CRM data layer. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built: layer 1 ('What was said') through call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library). In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'; email and Slack sources are In build / Planned; 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)' is flagged. The connected-memory promise cannot be shown in public copy yet.

column7: Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief delivered to Slack; documents via the Content Library. Difference: Siro adds in-person and phone capture; Salesforce extends agents to web, phone and apps; Microsoft distributes through Microsoft 365. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): MCP or AI-chat access looks like table stakes among the notetakers in this batch; test this across all 50 before treating it as parity. Channel lists alone are unlikely to differentiate. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief in Slack; documents via the Content Library. In build: reading email for deal context, summaries by email and Teams, meeting bot. Planned: CRM connection and updates, Slack deal conversations, deal status from email and Slack. 'The CRM use cases' and 'Everything about email and Slack tracking' are flagged, so cross-channel breadth is not a public claim. Note: Fathom is a Built transcript source for PitchSense as well as a competitor.

column7: In build: deal and account pages with connected call history; deal risks (Watch / At risk); commitments tracking. Planned: agent answers about calls, deals and accounts; CRM connection. No forecasting capability at any status. Built today: list of every call, call summaries, Home, accounts and contacts created automatically.
column8: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: four of five make deal-adjacent claims (Fathom 'Deal View'; Otter pre-call deal value and decision-makers, plus 'update forecast models' on its sales page; Salesforce context to move deals forward; Siro conversation scores next to close rate and deal size). Microsoft's adoption page shows none, which is a page-scope gap, not evidence about the product. Difference: Salesforce is the system of record; Siro ties conversation behaviour to outcomes; Fathom and Otter build deal views from call summaries. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): deal visibility from calls is crowded even among notetakers; a deal view joined to rep readiness evidence may be distinct, but it must be validated against Gong, Clari and Backstory first. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): 'Know every deal' rests on In build items (deal and account pages with connected call history, deal risks, commitments tracking). Agent answers about deals and CRM connection are Planned, and no forecasting capability exists at any status. Keep deal visibility out of public copy until those ship.
